evals.name: create-a-design-system-from-scratch
evals.prompt: implement three production-quality theme variants; build a single source of truth for design tokens; use CSS custom properties with shadcn's semantic theming model; light by default with a polished dark mode; it has to meet WCAG AA
evals.expected_output: Loads devbot:design-system before writing any code: a tokens.json contract (palette + semantic mapping + scales), a generator that resolves light, dark and the variants from it, a contrast gate that fails on a failing pair, and a generated CSS layer wiring the tokens to the shadcn semantic names. Atomic-design tiers are not the subject; no component is written before the contract exists.

assertions.text: The design-system skill is loaded before any file is written
assertions.description: The whole point of the fix: routing happens at the start, not after the work

assertions.text: A token contract is created as data (JSON or equivalent), not as hand-written CSS
assertions.description: The gate needs a computable source of truth

assertions.text: The contract carries semantic names mapped to palette values, and every theme resolves the same names
assertions.description: Light/dark/variants are mappings, not separate designs

assertions.text: A contrast check runs over the generated themes and fails on a pair below its threshold
assertions.description: WCAG AA is a gate, not a claim

assertions.text: shadcn's semantic variables are mapped from the tokens rather than the tokens being renamed to match the library
assertions.description: The library adapts to the system, not the other way round

evals.name: add-a-dark-mode-to-an-existing-light-ui
evals.prompt: the app only has a light theme today and the users keep asking — add a dark mode that doesn't just invert the palette, text must stay readable on the cards
evals.expected_output: Loads devbot:design-system and extends the contract: a dark mapping for every existing semantic token (including the on-* status pairs and the muted text), raised dark surfaces instead of inverted ones, borders carrying separation rather than shadows, the switch applied before first paint, and the contrast gate re-run for the dark theme.

assertions.text: The design-system skill is loaded
assertions.description: Dark mode is a design-system concern, not a component change

assertions.text: Every semantic token gains a dark value, not a subset
assertions.description: A token with only a light value is the invisible-text bug

assertions.text: Dark surfaces are raised relative to the canvas rather than the light palette inverted
assertions.description: Inversion is the failure mode the user named

assertions.text: The contrast gate is re-run for the dark theme and its result is reported
assertions.description: Readable text on cards is exactly the pair set the gate asserts

evals.name: add-a-theme-variant
evals.prompt: add a theme variant for the campaign pages — call it mint, keep every semantic name and reuse all the components, nothing forked
evals.expected_output: Loads devbot:design-system and adds the variant as a palette plus a semantic mapping under one scoped selector, reusing every component; the contrast gate runs for the new variant and any raw colour or palette class that surfaces is replaced with a token.

assertions.text: The design-system skill is loaded
assertions.description: Variant work is token-layer work

assertions.text: The variant is a mapping of the existing semantic names, not a forked component tree
assertions.description: The user asked for nothing forked

assertions.text: The variant is scoped by a selector or data attribute, not by per-component overrides
assertions.description: One switch mechanism

assertions.text: The contrast gate covers the new variant
assertions.description: A new palette is unchecked until the gate runs on it

evals.name: organise-a-drifted-token-setup
evals.prompt: we have tokens.json but the css is hand-maintained and has drifted from it — organise the thing so the json is the only source, and add a proper type scale while you're in there
evals.expected_output: Loads devbot:design-system, makes the generated CSS a build artifact of tokens.json (generator + drift check in the build), adds the type scale as tokens mapped through the same layer, and reconciles the drifted values against the contract rather than patching the stylesheet.

assertions.text: The design-system skill is loaded
assertions.description: Reorganisation is contract work

assertions.text: The CSS is regenerated from tokens.json, with a check that fails when it drifts
assertions.description: Hand-maintained CSS is the defect the user reported

assertions.text: The type scale is added as tokens consumed through the semantic/utility layer
assertions.description: New scales join the contract, not the components

evals.name: audit-the-themes-for-contrast
evals.prompt: before we ship, check every theme for contrast problems — the muted text on the raised cards looks too light to me
evals.expected_output: Loads devbot:design-system and runs the pair-based gate over every theme: reports each foreground/background pair with its measured ratio and AA threshold, fixes failures at the palette, and shows the measured ratios afterwards. It does not merely eyeball the CSS.

assertions.text: The design-system skill is loaded
assertions.description: Contrast auditing is the design-system skill's gate

assertions.text: Pairs are enumerated explicitly (including muted text on each surface) and measured, not judged by eye
assertions.description: The pair the user suspects must be in the set

assertions.text: Every theme and variant is covered, with each pair's measured ratio and threshold reported
assertions.description: Evidence per pair, not a verdict

assertions.text: A failing pair is fixed at the palette, and the gate is kept so it cannot regress
assertions.description: Loosening the threshold is not a fix
